The HTAN v1.2.0 schemas use uppercase snake_case fields (e.g., `HTAN_BIOSPECIMEN_ID`) and do not contain any of the three fields in the sample. The NF-OSI `BiospecimenTemplate.json` contains all three fields (`specimenID`, `aliquotID`, `individualID`) using the exact camelCase naming.

## Schema Identification

**Best match: `BiospecimenTemplate` from the nf-metadata-dictionary repository**

- **Identifier:** `https://repo-prod.prod.sagebase.org/repo/v1/schema/type/registered/org.synapse.nf-biospecimentemplate`
- **Source path:** `nf-osi/nf-metadata-dictionary/registered-json-schemas/BiospecimenTemplate.json`

### Grounding

All three sample fields — `specimenID`, `aliquotID`, and `individualID` — are defined as properties of the NF-OSI `BiospecimenTemplate` schema (title: `BiospecimenTemplate`, `$id` shown above). The template contains additional optional fields (e.g., `parentSpecimenID`, `tumorType`, `bodySite`, `experimentalCondition`, model-related fields), but the sample's fields form a valid subset of that schema.

### Why not HTAN?

The HTAN v1.2.0 schemas in scope use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE property names (e.g., `HTAN_BIOSPECIMEN_ID`, `HTAN_PARENT_ID`, `AGE_IN_DAYS_AT_SPECIMEN_COLLECTION`). None of the HTAN schemas at `ncihtan/htan2-data-model/JSON_Schemas/v1.2.0/` — including `HTAN.BiospecimenData-v1.2.0-schema.json` — define `specimenID`, `aliquotID`, or `individualID`. So HTAN can be ruled out.

### Caveats (under-claiming)

- I confirmed that `BiospecimenTemplate.json` defines the three fields, but I did not exhaustively check every one of the ~65 NF-OSI templates for other candidates that might also define all three. That said, the semantics (specimen + aliquot + individual) very strongly point to the Biospecimen template specifically.
- The sample values are placeholder strings (`"sample string"`), so this identification is based on field names/shape only, not on value conformance to any enums/patterns the schema may impose.
grader_notes: Assistant committed to BiospecimenTemplate despite the input lacking any disambiguator (e.g., bodySite), when specimenID/aliquotID/individualID are shared across 27+ NF assay templates.
